answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind cryptographic attestation chains to recursive zero-knowledge proofs that verify unique compute lineage. Registering each identity demands staking a bond that scales superlinearly: a single node deposits a modest jade token, but replicating swarms triggers exponential capital exhaustion. Even an agent executing a covert whisper within a distant nebula cannot counterfeit root proofs without facing ruinous staking curves.
